provenance: Each observation is explicitly classified as PURE_XNA_DERIVED metadata or RUBY_MAPPING_QUALIFICATION; never CNA output
derivation: Foundation 45 Game.IsActive. Contract rows are read from the pinned XNA 4.0 Windows metadata of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game.dll and from the Microsoft-free IL inventory derived from it; the two GamerServices terms are derived from Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GamerServices.dll. Game::get_IsActive is thirty bytes and is not a field read: it initialises a local to false, calls GamerServicesDispatcher::get_IsInitialized and, only when that is true, assigns Guide::get_IsVisible to the local; it then loads isActive and returns false when that is false, and otherwise returns the local compared with zero. So the property is isActive && !(GamerServicesDispatcher.IsInitialized && Guide.IsVisible), and the guard is the only reason it never throws, because Guide::get_IsVisible throws InvalidOperationException(GamerServicesNotInitialized) when the dispatcher is not initialised and otherwise answers isVisible || forceGuideVisible. GamerServicesDispatcher::get_IsInitialized is packetBuffer != null. The backing field isActive is written in exactly two places in the whole assembly, Game::HostActivated and Game::HostDeactivated, each of which returns early when the field already holds the value it would write, writes the field, and only then raises OnActivated or OnDeactivated -- which is why the property is already true inside an Activated handler. Nothing else writes it, so a Game that has never run reports the CLR default false.
